what: trainer-diag-relay.yml's commit-back step is `git push origin HEAD:${{ github.ref_name }}` under `set -euo pipefail`, with no rebase and no retry. When a second relay triggered by the SAME push (board-post.yml, pr-opener.yml) commits to the branch first, the relay's push is a non-fast-forward, the step fails, and a result it had ALREADY COMPUTED on the trainer is discarded. Measured 2026-09-07 (MI-154b): request mi154b-scalp-probe-20260907 produced no result after a push that also carried automation/board-posts/; board-post committed 228f2719 first and the relay lost the race. Re-sent ALONE under a fresh name, the identical script returned state=ran remote_exit=0 in ~30s. WHY IT IS WORSE THAN A LOST RUN: the failure presents as an ABSENT result file, byte-identical to 'the relay never fired' and to 'the trainer is unreachable' -- three faults with three different remedies collapsed into one silent state, and the natural first suspicion is the trainer's health, which was fine throughout. It cost ~25 minutes of misdiagnosis. All three push-triggered relays (trainer-diag-relay, board-post, pr-opener) share this commit-back shape, so any two triggered by one push can collide.
